description: This episode explores the Meselson-Stahl experiment of 1958, which definitively proved that DNA replicates semi-conservatively—each new double helix contains one original strand and one newly synthesized strand. Using elegant isotope labeling and density gradient centrifugation, the experiment resolved a fundamental question about heredity and completed the century-long quest to understand how genetic information is faithfully copied and passed down through generations. Essential listening for anyone interested in molecular biology, experimental design, or the history of genetics.
